H_hierarchical.evidence: Section 5.2 defines a flat set of five modes S1-S5 and Figure 7 is a flat transition diagram; no parent/child or composite states are described.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transition events such as I2/I3 depend on constraint satisfaction and obstacle/no-fly detection; the paper defines multi-variable arithmetic constraints including radar distance, no-fly-zone distance, collision distance, and communication distance inequalities.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: On radar-threat reconfiguration, the controller selects the most suitable/nearest UAV for interference, solves its best interference position in real time, updates the desired formation parameters for other UAVs, and sends the next mode to DMPC for control output.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: No explicit fault, emergency stop, rollback, or recovery transition is specified; radar and no-fly responses are mission threat-avoidance modes rather than a fault model.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State names and trigger labels are in Section 5.2, arithmetic safety constraints are defined earlier in Sections 3-4, and concrete transition timing appears later in Table 5.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Domain terms such as no-fly zone, radar threat, and cooperative interference are accompanied by explicit formulas or prose behavior, so no outside-domain transition rule is required.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The S1-S5/I1-I9 list only names modes and events; S4 actions such as selecting an interference UAV and solving formation parameters are described later in narrative prose.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: Guards/constraints include expressions over multiple variables, e.g. radar distance inequalities, h_adr1/h_adr2, d_ij >= D_safe, and d_ij <= D_com.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite state or parent state with internal behavior is present.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The paper does not declare a from-any-state fault or recovery transition; avoidance transitions are ordinary mode transitions.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The sample has several arithmetic and boolean guard/constraint families over UAV position, radar geometry, collision distance, communication distance, speed, and heading bounds.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: No clear single cross-cutting rule over several substates or parent-level during aspect is declared.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The FSM outputs an abstract next formation mode to the DMPC controller, decoupling mode selection from concrete velocity/course control, though most effects are still control-specific.

key_nl_quotes: FSM formation management unit will make the formation mode of the next step and transfer it to DMPC formation controller
the formation goes into S4 ... select the most suitable UAV ... obtain the best position to interfere
one_line_pitch: A flat but guard- and action-heavy UAV formation manager that forces models to connect high-level FSM events with multi-variable threat constraints and narrative reconfiguration actions.
rationale: This is not a hierarchy or fault-recovery stress case, but it is strong on the two weakest baseline components of guards and actions. The paper separates state/event definitions, mathematical constraints, and prose actions across sections, creating a high baseline-trap density. It is suitable as a top candidate for testing whether an LLM method can recover semantically rich guarded transitions and non-trivial transition behavior from industrial control prose.
